findings.issue_text: Malformed Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses z.string().toString() which evaluates to a nonsense key instead of a dynamic key matcher; schema does not validate what the comment claims
refresh_token is set to literal string "refresh_token" when missing from token response, which will corrupt stored credentials and fail future refresh attempts
Type/shape mismatch in refreshOAuthTokens return value: sync-disabled returns adapter-specific shapes while sync-enabled returns a fetch Response, breaking callers that destructure res.data
refreshOAuthTokens has return type any, hiding the return shape mismatch
Webhook endpoint lacks req.method === "POST" check, accepting GET/PUT/etc.
Webhook endpoint uses Zod parse() instead of safeParse(), causing unhandled 500 with potential stack trace leakage on malformed payloads
Webhook endpoint calls JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) unguarded; decryption or parse failure crashes the handler
Webhook secret comparison uses !== which is timing-unsafe; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual
Salesforce CalendarService refreshes token unconditionally on every instantiation regardless of token expiry, causing wasteful network round-trips
Salesforce uses response.statusText !== "OK" for error detection, which is deprecated/unreliable (HTTP/2 drops it) and localized in some clients
Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, potentially associating tokens with the wrong user
Dead code in Salesforce CalendarService after parseRefreshTokenResponse throws; the if (!accessTokenParsed.success) check is unreachable
No unit tests added for parseRefreshTokenResponse, refreshOAuthTokens, or the new webhook handler

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens has return type any, hiding the return shape mismatch

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `refreshOAuthTokens` is declared with very loose types (`refreshFunction: () => any` and no explicit return type), and it can return two incompatible shapes depending on the branch. In the sync branch it returns the result of `fetch(...)` (a `Response`), while in the normal branch it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns (often a parsed token object or a client-specific response). Call sites assume specific shapes: e.g. HubSpot assigns `HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, but if syncing is enabled it will receive a `Response` instead of a `HubspotToken` object; Google Calendar expects `res?.data` but a `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`. Stronger typing would surface this mismatch at compile time; the current `any` hides a likely runtime bug when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook endpoint lacks req.method === "POST" check, accepting GET/PUT/etc.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler processes requests without checking `req.method`. There is no guard like `if (req.method !== "POST") return res.status(405)...`, so Next.js will route GET/PUT/etc. into the same logic path. This is verifiable in the diff and can lead to incorrect behavior (e.g., non-POST requests hitting zod `parse(req.body)` and throwing) and unnecessarily exposing the endpoint to unintended methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook endpoint calls JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) unguarded; decryption or parse failure crashes the handler

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` without any try/catch or validation. If `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing/incorrect, `symmetricDecrypt(...)` can throw or return non-JSON, and `JSON.parse(...)` will throw on invalid JSON. Either case will bubble up and crash the handler (resulting in a 500) rather than returning a controlled error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED evaluates to string | undefined, not boolean; type leaks into boolean contexts

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` being imported from `@calcom/lib/constants` and used in boolean conditions (e.g., `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)`). It does not show how that constant is defined or typed. Without seeing its declaration/type, we cannot verify that it is `string | undefined` (or that this change introduces a type leak/TS error). The usage itself is valid for either a boolean or a truthy/falsy string, so the proposed finding is not directly verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: symmetricDecrypt called with || "" fallback silently passes empty key to decrypt function if CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset, causing cryptic error or garbage output

adjudication.rationale:
In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, decryption is done via:

```ts
symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")
```

If `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is unset/misconfigured, the code explicitly falls back to an empty string and proceeds to decrypt + `JSON.parse(...)` with no validation/guard. This can lead to runtime exceptions (decrypt/JSON parse) or incorrect output rather than a clear configuration error, and will surface as an unhandled error (likely 500) since there’s no try/catch around it. So the finding points to a real, verifiable robustness/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Double await in HubSpot CalendarService: inner await is redundant inside an async arrow whose result is awaited by the caller

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, HubspotCalendarService wraps `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)` in `async () => await ...` when passing it to `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. The inner `await` is redundant because an `async` function already wraps the returned promise, and `refreshOAuthTokens` awaits the `refreshFunction()` result anyway. However, this does not change behavior or introduce a bug/security/correctness issue; it is a minor style/performance nit at most.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook endpoint validates body after auth checks; consider validating before DB lookup

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the request body is validated with `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` **before** any Prisma DB lookups (`prisma.user.findUnique`, `prisma.app.findUnique`, etc.). The code does perform auth checks (feature flag + webhook secret) before parsing, but the proposed finding claims validation happens after auth checks and implies this affects DB lookup ordering; it does not—DB lookups are already after validation. This is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff, more of a preference about whether to parse before auth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zoho Bigin redirect URI changed from appConfig.slug to literal "zoho-bigin", which will break silently if appConfig.slug ever differs

adjudication.rationale: The diff provided does not show any changes related to Zoho Bigin, redirect URIs, or any usage of appConfig.slug vs a literal "zoho-bigin". The only app slugs visible in the changes are for google-calendar, hubspot, lark-calendar, office365-calendar, msteams, etc. Since the claimed change is not present in the diff, the finding is not verifiable and therefore not a real issue identified in this patch.
